content.title: European steelmakers' shares rise on EU plan to cut steel quotas
content.summary:
STORY: Shares in European steelmakers rose in early Wednesday trade.

Investors bought up after the European Commission proposed cutting tariff-free steel import quotas by almost half.

It's part of a plan to preserve viable steelmaking in the EU.

EU steel producers are operating at only 67% of their capacity due to rising imports and U.S. tariffs.

The new measures are designed to push that up towards 80%.

ArcelorMittal said on Tuesday it was "relieved" by the Commission's proposal.

Thyssenkrupp also said in written statements it supported the plan, while Aperam welcomed the measures Wednesday.

Thyssenkrupp said the Commission recognized the European steel industry and its associated value chains were in serious danger without effective trade protection.

Industry data shows some 5.5 million jobs in Germany are directly or indirectly tied to the steel industry.

J.P. Morgan analysts said the proposed import quota cuts could lower steel imports into the EU by 8 metric tons.

They argue this could positively affect local steel producers' pricing power.

But European carmakers have concerns.

The European Automobile Manufacturers' Association warned about the inflationary impact tighter restrictions could have on steel imports.
